subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary external plugins be allowed to invoke other plugins' Gateway methods, and if so through which caller-attributed and allowlisted Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary; automation cannot safely choose whether raw dispatch, curated capabilities, or trusted-only access is the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Design an allowlisted external-plugin contract
options.body: Expose only approved plugin methods or typed capabilities with caller identity, authorization checks, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep Gateway calls trusted-only
options.body: Leave `api.runtime.gateway.request` limited to bundled or trusted official plugins and ask external plugins to use existing HTTP routes or future typed service seams.

options.title: Reject inter-plugin Gateway RPCs
options.body: Close this direction and require plugin authors to publish shared services or parse documented outputs outside the Gateway RPC surface.

recommendation.title: Design an allowlisted external-plugin contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved plugin methods or typed capabilities with caller identity, authorization checks, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current route-scoped Gateway dispatch contract and is the strongest history match for the security-boundary decision.
